title: Kannauj-Varman Dynasty
capsule: The Varman dynasty of Kannauj was a ruling line in the upper Gangetic plain that held the city of Kannauj—a prestige seat contested among north Indian powers—in the period following the collapse of Harsha's empire in 647. The dynasty is attested through copper-plate grants and appears in the context of the tripartite struggle (Tripartite Struggle) among the Gurjara-Pratiharas, the Palas of Bengal, and the Rashtrakutas of the Deccan, each of whom sought control of Kannauj as a symbol of imperial legitimacy. The historical record for this dynasty is thin, and its rulers, dates, and territorial extent are reconstructed primarily from epigraphic fragments and the accounts of later chroniclers.

This dynasty is poorly attested; the territorial assignment is highly uncertain and rests on fragmentary copper-plate evidence rather than any systematic cartographic or narrative record.
